items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: You know you want to sound like Clifford Brown? There’s probably every song he’s ever played already transcribed.

ctx.x: Um hum. Very interesting. The other day I heard John Coltrane’s “A Love Supreme” part of it. They played part of it on Sirius radio. And I started thinking about the certain decades of jazz. And it seems like for much of jazz there was a social connection that went with the music and I’m not sure I’m correct about this but in the 30s you had a dance and entertainment element. In the 50s — when I think of the 50s I think of you know there’s this sort of hipster — Dizzy Gillespie with the beret, like there’s a hip-…

Yeah. People often ask me where is jazz going. And I said you need to ask young people because they have their finger on the pulse of the music. They know everything is coming out, they know that. So I don’t know if I’m even qualified to answer that. And I agree with you about the 60s. In a joking way I say yeah the jazz universe peaked in ’65 you know. When everybody was alive and well. You know, Ben Webster was alive and well. Coleman Hawkins was alive and well. Sonny Rollins doing his thing. John Coltrane…

playing music for social reasons I wonder. But I can say this though the world has gone so materialistic. How many things can they have? Let’s get some more things. Things, things, things. But for musicians, just to play music, that’s pretty amazing.
